Hey friends, for years the word sales genuinely gave me the ick. So I sat down with my friend and mentor Daniel Priestley, who has done thousands of sales meetings, to break down his zero-pressure sales system. We do a full live roleplay where Dan sells me on ScoreApp, then I throw every objection I can think of at him (too expensive, bad timing, let me think about it) and we unpack what was going on in his head at each step. videos.title: Falling in Love Is Rebellion | Robert Greene
videos.description:
I’ve long been a fan of Robert Greene’s books, and indeed have recommended Mastery any time someone asks me for a positively life-changing book suggestion.

Recently, I sat down with him on the Huberman Lab podcast to discuss his latest book: Law of the Sublime. It’s absolutely incredible. And the discussion we had on the podcast is absolutely one of my favorite of all time.

Robert Greene is an expert on human nature, individual expression and personal growth. On the podcast and in his new book he explains the sublime—what it is and how to access it: in relationships, work, through observation, expression and more.

What emerges is a larger conversation about human consciousness, perception and ensuring your life is lived and experienced to the fullest.

Thank you @RobertGreeneOfficial for the incredible works you’ve put into the world and for being a guest on the podcast once again. It was an honor and a pleasure!

Thanks for Robert, this is a podcast you won’t want to miss!

Disclaimer & Disclosures: https://www.hubermanlab.com/disclaimer

You’ve probably lied to someone today. You also probably think you lie less than everyone else. Welp, I have some bad news. We all manipulate, we all get played, and sometimes, the smarter you are, the easier you are to con.

In this episode, Drew and I get into what manipulation is, why everyone does it, and how to keep from getting fooled. We tell the story of how Freud’s nephew turned bacon into a doctor-approved breakfast, and how the TSA spent nearly $1 billion training officers to spot liars, with nothing to show for it. We walk through the one test that shows when persuasion crosses into manipulation, and the tactics advertisers, propagandists, and con artists have been running on you for a century. Then we cover why skeptics make some of the easiest marks and the only defense with serious evidence behind it.

We also spend a good chunk of time on the manipulator you know best (or least)... yourself.

You can’t fully escape influence, and you might not want to. But once you know the playbook, you’ll spot it, even when it’s coming from inside the house.
